title: Pelican Retail quick hypothesis & outbound play
content:
Context:
- Pelican is a mid-market retail platform focusing on SMB merchants (POS + online storefront).
- They surfaced interest during a merchant-facing summit; tech lead (Ari Gold) responded to an ask about faster invoice summarization and returns automation.
- Likely pain: spikes around holiday sales -> unpredictable cost and latency; wants predictable inference for chat/returns triage.
- Current stack: AWS-hosted, mix of in-house heuristics + vendor NLU (blackbox) for routing.

Hypothesis (what we can sell quickly):
1) Pilot: embed a small LLM endpoint to power returns triage + canned responses (30–60k queries/day peak) with predictable latency SLA.
2) Differentiators to emphasize: predictable tail latency, cost controls (batching / caching), private deployment option for PII-sensitive returns metadata.
3) Success metric: reduce manual returns handling time by 30% and reduce average latency to <300ms for top 95th pct requests.

Key stakeholders (mapped, need confirmation):
- Ari Gold (tech lead, integration) — engineering champion?
- Mina Cho (ops lead, customer support) — cares about MTTR, ticket volume, training data hygiene
- CFO / Head of Finance (TBD) — cares about unit economics (cost / ticket)
- CISO (possible blocker) — needs KMS/HSM + audit logs for private data

Quick discovery notes (from call + notes):
- Ari: "we need something that doesn't blow up our bill during the holidays".
- Mina: "if it can cut our returns triage time that's huge — we have seasonal temps who rely on scripts".
- They store PII in returns notes; need to understand compliance requirements (PCI scope?).

Outbound approach (sequence draft):
1) Email 1 (warm intro - short)
   Subject: Quick idea to cut Pelican returns time by 30%
   Body: Hi Ari — I was inspired by your summit question — quick idea: a short pilot to offload returns triage to an LLM endpoint with predictable latency and capped cost. 2–3 week setup, we can co-design prompts and give you a cost/latency dashboard. Interested in 15 min?

2) Email 2 (value + technical + ROI) 4 days later
   - Call out expected token/unit spend, an example throughput profile (peak 60k/day), and a conservative pricing estimate (dedicated pool vs hosted).
   - Include a one-pager with pilot scope and success metrics.

3) LinkedIn + Slack nudge between emails (peer-level)

Sample objection flows / responses (short):
- Objection: "We can't expose PII to external APIs."
  -> Response: "We can run the pilot on Dedicated or Private (VPC) with KMS controls and audit logs; we can sign an NDA and configure token redaction. Also propose an initial synthetic data test to prove process."
- Objection: "Cost is unpredictable."
  -> Response: "We can cap spend with committed Dedicated capacity and set automatic fallbacks to a cheaper model variant; Redwood Optimize will give batching/quantization recs upfront so you know unit cost before go-live."
- Objection: "We already have a rules engine."
  -> Response: "Pilot doesn't replace rules; it augments — handle the messy, free-text cases and escalate low-confidence hits back to your rules + human queue. Quick win: reduce manual tickets for the long tail."

Pilot scoping (minimal viable):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2w integration + 2w live + 2w optimization + wrap-up)
- Traffic: route 10% of returns initially (A/B split) — expect 2–4k/day to start
- Deliverables: integration code, prompt set, eval harness (precision/recall on labeled sample), SLA doc, cost projection, handoff runbook

Pricing sketch (to iterate with finance):
- Hosted pilot (fast): $X committed credits (placeholder) + per-token usage. Pros: quick setup. Cons: less control.
- Dedicated pilot (recommended if they care about spend predictability): monthly reserved pool sized for peak + overage rules.
- Private (enterprise): platform license + deployment package

Metrics to track (dashboard suggestions):
- Per-request latency distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- Tokens per request, cost per ticket, tickets deflected to automation
- False positive rate (incorrect auto-responses) and escalation ratio
- Ops MTTR before/after

Play testing ideas (internal):
- Synthetic dataset: sample returns text from support logs (anonymize) -> evaluate on 2000 samples.
- Prompt variants A/B: conservative (send short template + ask to extract fields) vs freeform (generate full reply). Compare accuracy + token usage.
- Fallback policy: if confidence < threshold -> route to human + log label for retraining

Immediate next steps (owner):
- [Sofia] Draft Email1 and one-pager by EOD Wed (linked artifacts: GH PR template)
- [Marco] Confirm whether we can offer a 30-day limited Dedicated slot for pilot (ask infra)
- [Jaya] Pull anonymized sample returns logs (500 entries) and scrub PII for evaluation dataset
- Schedule 30m sync with Ari + Mina (aim: week of Nov 24)

Open questions / risks:
- Compliance appetite: is PCI in scope? need to ask security.
- Data access latency: their returns pipeline may have attachments (images) — what counts as required for MVP?
- Who signs the MSA? Legal timeline could push pilot out 6–8 weeks.

Casual notes to self (brainstorm voice):
- Try an example subject line that calls out measurable improvement — merchants respond to % reduction in ops time.
- Could offer an onboarding credit for the first 2 months to offset trust barrier.
- If they love it, next upsell: embed in checkout to reduce chargebacks (higher value).

Slack copy (short nudge to Ari):
- "Hey Ari — quick idea from our summit chat. 15m to show a low-effort pilot to cut returns triage time? We can scope a 6-week pilot with metrics + cost projection. Sofia/Marco to adapt to your timeline"

Draft email (for copy-paste):
- Hi Ari — following up from the summit. Quick idea: we can run a 6-week pilot to automate part of Pelican's returns triage with predictable latency (p95 < 300ms) and a capped spend. We co-design prompts and give you a dashboard showing cost + accuracy. Would you be open to a 15m intro next week?

End.
